newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil FEBEC fair voice for coffee council - trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil FEBEC fair voice for coffee council - trade.

text.p: The choice of Brazil's Coffee Exporters' Federation as the sector's representative body on a new coffee policy-making council does not mean an alternative exporters' association has no voice, traders said.

Rather members of the Brazil Coffee Exporters' Association (Abecafe) will still be able to express their views but within the Febec structure, given the federation is made up of six regional coffee centers to which Abecafe companies belong.
"Now exporters will have to sort out differences within the Febec system rather than compete with it," one dealer said.
"Abecafe members still are part of FEBEC even if they do not choose to be but it doesn't work the other way round," he added.

Abecafe's president Jorge Esteve said he was disappointed today with the decision to set up a council with 12 members, six each from the public and private sectors but which included only one place for a exporter representative from Febec.

Abecafe, which was set up last year after certain companies refused to sign a private sector plan dividing out coffee exports internally, now has 40 member firms whose exports accounted for around 40 percent of the 1.56 million bags of coffee shipped in August, according to Febec statistics.

Representative from Abecafe members recently won recent elections for the board of the Santos Commercial Association, which means they now have the possibility of electing an Abecafe member as vice-president of Febec, the Febec president said.
"From January 1, the Santos Association will nominate some else which should be somebody of that faction because they won the election," said Oswaldo Aranha.

"There's nothing wrong with Abecafe continuing to exist...But the government wanted a smaller council which was representative and they had to decide which entities they believed would be most representative in the future," he added.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
